data.gender_notes: Maaliki is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who owns, the one in charge, the master. The name Maaliki carries the meaning “The Owner” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Maaliki usually hope their child will grow to embody the owner and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the ultimate power of Allah, the owner of all creation
data.etymology: Maaliki belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Owner.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maaliki total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Maaliki holds a significant cultural impact in the Islamic world, particularly in the context of various religious and literary traditions. In Sufism, the mystical branch of Islam, Maaliki represents the concept of divine ownership and the belief that all things belong to God. It is also associated with the idea of the custodian or caretaker of knowledge and wisdom, as found in the famous Madani and Maliki schools of Islamic jurisprudence.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Maaliki holds deep significance in emphasizing the belief in God's ultimate control and ownership over all things, and the importance of striving to serve and please Him as the true Master and Sustainer. It also highlights the responsibility of individuals to be the caretakers and keepers of knowledge, moral values, and spiritual truths, reflecting the Muslim ideal of being both productive members of society and seekers on the path to God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "The Owner" symbolizes The one who owns, the one in charge, the master. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Maaliki serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of the owner.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abi Dunya reported that Malik ibn Anas was asked about the ruling of a man who had intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating. Malik replied, 'The sin is upon the man.' This statement of Malik's became the foundation for the doctrines of the Maliki School of Islamic Law.
historical_references.context: Early development of Maliki School of Islamic Law in North Africa

historical_references.reference: Malik ibn Anas was a prominent scholar of the Islamic faith in Umayyad Spain. He is considered the founder of the Maliki School of Islamic Law, and his rulings were influential in shaping the legal system of the Islamic world. Malik's legal decisions were based on the customs and practices of the people of Medina, which he studied during a visit there.
historical_references.context: Establishment and spread of Maliki School of Islamic Law in Spain
